Pt received dose 1 of Pfizer vaccine on 4/15/21 at approx. 3:46pm at a clinic due to past allergies. While being monitored for 30 minutes post vaccine, pt complained of slight wheeze, pain in throat and tongue feeling heavy. Only visible sign was small red blotches on upper chest. BP was 159/95, pulse 75 and pulse ox was 97%. 25 mg Benadryl po  given at approx. 4:16pm. Pt remained at clinic to be monitored. At 4:50pm, patient left with husband feeling much improved: throat pain gone, wheeze gone, tongue feeling normal, swallows easily and red areas on chest visible, but diminished in size. Patient called on 4/16/21 and no further complaints. Felt much improved once home and no further symptoms. Encouraged to let staff know about incident when receiving dose 2 and to stay longer than 30 minutes for monitoring.

I had some fatigue, but otherwise felt fine. I went to the Emergency Department on April11th thinking that my INR was too high since I?m on a blood thinner medication. The ER did an ultrasound of my legs and no blood clots were found. They did a CBC and I had a platelet count of 6,000. They admitted me, gave me a platelet transfusion and a steroid injection. They discharged me from the hospital on 04/12/2021 on 60 mg of Prednisone and to follow up with my hematologist, MD. My platelet count has since returned to normal.  I am having a CBC once a week and tapering off the Prednisone. Both Dr. and my Rheumatologist, MD believe that my severe drop in platelets were due to the Covid vaccine causing my Lupus to become very active and attack my platelets.  Please feel free to contact me if you have any additional questions. Thanks you,

I received my second dose of Pfizer around 3pm on Sunday, April 4 2021. By about midnight, I had a fever and the fever/headache and exhaustion persisted throughout Monday. I did not take any medicine. By Tuesday morning, my fever broke, but I developed a large 6 inch rash under my left armpit (my second shot was in my right arm as I am left handed). By Tuesday afternoon, I had developed a bad cough. Given that I work remotely, and had only been to a grocery store (double masked) with my mother a few days prior to the second dose, I assumed the cough was a result of the second dose. My cough become worse, and by Wednesday it sounded like bronchitis so I went to my doctor. She believed that it was a bronchitis cough, had me tested for viral infections, and put me on a variety of medications from antibiotics to steroids and inhalers. I tested negative for all the respiratory illnesses I was tested for, as well as COVID-19. The medications did not seem to help, and my doctor added another inhaler and medication to the mix. After about 2 weeks of medications and no improvements, my doctor had me get a chest X-ray to make sure I didn?t have pneumonia or any other obstruction in my lungs. I also stopped all medication on Tuesday, April 20. My chest X-ray came back clear later that week, and I decided to just stay off all medications and hope that my body would self heal, since this seemed to be a self created bronchitis, as my parents did not get sick. Finally, after 2 weeks and 4 days, my cough has improved significantly to the point where I can now talk almost normally, without going into coughing spasms and feeling as though it was difficult to breathe.
